title: Assignments
text:
Unless otherwise stated, you may work on assignments individually or in pairs, and your choice may change from one assignment to the next.
For each assignment, I will create a group set in Canvas; you will sign up to form your group.
Only one person per group submits the assignment in Canvas. The submission is automatically shared with all group members.
Grades and feedback are shared with the whole group. By default, all members receive the same grade.
Assignments are due by 11:59 PM Chicago Time on the due date. Canvas displays due dates in your time zone.
Each submission must include all relevant files:

A self-contained, working copy of any code used.
A PDF version of item 1, including the output, plus any analytical work. Legible handwriting and typed work are both acceptable. You may embed analytical work as Markdown in the code.

title: Welcome to MATH 332
text:
Course Description
This course develops the theory and applications of linear algebra through systems of equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and inner product spaces. Python will support visualization, numerical computation, symbolic computation, and experimentation.


Instructor: Fred J. Hickernell



Office: Galvin Tower 18C3-1
Office hours: By appointment (book here)
Phone: 312-567-8983
Email: hickernell@illinoistech.edu
Website     LinkedIn     Google Scholar     Mathematics Genealogy Profile

Brief bio: Fred J. Hickernell is professor of applied mathematics. His research focuses on improving the efficiency of computer simulations and developing justifiable stopping criteria. He has spent most of his career at Hong Kong Baptist University and Illinois Institute of Technology, often in academic administrative roles. He has served on the editorial boards of the Journal of Complexity, Mathematics of Computation, and the SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics and the recipient of the 2016 Joseph F. Traub Prize for Achievement in Information-Based Complexity.
Hickernell speaks Cantonese and enjoys Chinese food. He is married with adult children. He enjoys discussing matters of substance. His most important identity is a disciple of Jesus.

title: Accessing the Course Repository
text: The course repository contains the website source, slides, notebooks, assets, and a shared-library submodule. Students should treat the instructor’s repository as read-only. Coursework will not be submitted through Git.

title: Accessing the Course Repository
text:
Prerequisites
Install Git and choose either HTTPS or SSH authentication for GitHub.

title: Accessing the Course Repository
text:
Clone the repository
Choose one method.

HTTPS
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/fjhickernell/MATH332Fall2026.git
cd MATH332Fall2026


SSH
git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:fjhickernell/MATH332Fall2026.git
cd MATH332Fall2026






Note



The GitHub repository link will become usable after the repository is published. Until then, these commands document the intended setup.

title: Accessing the Course Repository
text:
Verify the submodule
git submodule status
If classlib was not initialized, run:
git submodule update --init --recursive

title: Accessing the Course Repository
text:
Get course updates
From the repository directory, run:
git pull --ff-only
git submodule update --init --recursive
The second command checks out the shared library version recorded by the course repository. Do not use git submodule update --remote unless the instructor explicitly requests it.

title: Accessing the Course Repository
text:
If you have local changes
Check your work before updating:
git status
Copy important work outside the course repository or commit it to your own private repository before pulling updates. Ask for help rather than discarding changes you want to keep.

title: Jupyter Notebooks
text: Course notebooks provide executable demonstrations and exercises for numerical matrix computation, exact symbolic computation, visualization, and experimentation.

title: Jupyter Notebooks
text:
Demonstrations
Instructor demonstrations illustrate linear algebra concepts and connect algebraic calculations with geometric interpretation.

Matrix Computation: NumPy and SymPy — a companion to Lecture 00 introducing numerical and exact matrix calculations, linear systems, least squares, and responsible computation
Systems and Matrices — a placeholder companion to Lecture 01 that will develop Gaussian elimination, solution-set comparisons, and the resistance-network exercise

title: Jupyter Notebooks
text:
Exercises
Student exercises will provide opportunities to explore matrices, vector spaces, transformations, eigenvalues, and inner products computationally. Exercise notebooks will be linked here after they have been developed and validated.
